title: Fixed Orthogonal Seven Roll Banks and Guide Eyes Wire Straightener
description: One newly authored whole empty two-plane wire-straightener-inspired benchtop assembly. A complete low chamfered long bed supports a full upright rear carrier plate on the left and a separate complete raised horizontal carrier plate on the right. Seven complete short circumferentially grooved rolls alternate above and below an empty feed axis in the left bank; seven independent full grooved rolls alternate to either side in the perpendicular right bank. Every roll has its own full fixed shaft and entire mount block; three complete adjustment-stem and hand-knob exteriors rise above the upright plate and three project behind the horizontal plate. Two whole end brackets carry genuinely open round guide eyes along the empty straight centreline. Unlike the old wire stripper there is no single lower feed roll beneath a raised cutting disc, tall two-cheek top-bridge frame or side crank. Unlike the sheet slip roller there are no three full-width long rolls spanning paired end cheeks. Unlike the coil winder there is no central winding bobbin, drive handwheel, traverse rail or guide-eye carriage. No old whole model or extracted machine component geometry reused, no input wire or purported processed result. All mesh coordinates and whole support organization newly authored together. One whole static model zero scenes, four constant opaque untextured PBR roles, native metres Z up. Simplified empty machinery category art, not a functional straightening device: no wire engagement, plastic deformation, drive, synchronized adjustment, roll hardness, precision, axis tolerance, usable material diameter, capacity, manufacture, engineering or safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation, interaction or text.
